what_it_does: Running a 'mixture-of-experts' (MoE) AI model — one where each input token is routed to only a few specialist sub-networks rather than the whole network — is tricky on a machine that has both a CPU and a GPU, because most of the specialists' weights must be stored in cheaper CPU memory and fetched on demand. The problem is that which specialists get activated is hard to predict, so a naive system either wastes time waiting or brings the wrong data over. HybriMoE attacks this with three coordinated ideas: it re-decides each layer which parts of the computation go to the CPU versus the GPU based on what's actually active at that moment; it uses the current layer's 'routing scores' (the numbers that pick specialists) to guess which specialists the next layer will need, so it can start fetching them early; and it keeps a small cache of the most valuable specialists and 'running notes' (key-value cache — the model's memory of tokens seen so far) in fast GPU memory, prioritized by how often and how importantly they are used. Together these cut idle waiting on a resource-constrained CPU-GPU system.
